items.title: FuelPin Tcool must see Channel.Tavg
items.description: In single and series Channel/FuelPin plants, a FuelPin's Tcool input must be driven by the corresponding Channel.Tavg output, not Channel.Tin, Channel.Tout, FuelPin.Tc, FuelPin.Tf, or a boundary Const. This is inferred from the port table and conservation coupling: the fuel pin needs the bulk/average coolant temperature for heat transfer while the channel computes Tavg from Tin and Q_fuel. Episode 6 succeeded with connect(ch.Tavg, fp.Tcool) and connect(tin.y, ch.Tin); episode 4 failed when fp.Tcool was driven by tin.y and ch.Tin by fp.Tc.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin temperatures or channel outlet/average temperatures are offset; Tcool or Tin is driven by a non-bulk temperature source.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin/Channel pair, verify the thermal feedback connection is connect(<channel>.Tavg, <fuelpin>.Tcool), and verify the channel inlet is driven by the upstream boundary or previous Channel.Tout, not by a FuelPin output.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect Channel.Tin to FuelPin.Tcool; Channel.Tin is an input and cannot drive another input.
Do not use Channel.Tout as FuelPin.Tcool unless a task explicitly defines that nonstandard coupling; it can create over-determination or wrong heat-transfer temperature.
Do not drive Channel.Tin from FuelPin.Tc or FuelPin.Tf; those are solid temperatures, not coolant inlet boundary conditions.

items.title: PowerSource drives FuelPin.Q_fission only
items.description: In these nuclear thermal-hydraulic plants, PowerSource.P is a heat-generation signal and must drive FuelPin.Q_fission, not Channel.Tin or Channel.Q_fuel. Episode 2 initially had ps2.P connected to ch3.Tin and ch2.Tout connected to fp2.Q_fission, producing temperatures equal to 2.4e+09 and inconsistent initialization; success came after routing ps2.P to fp2.Q_fission and ch2.Tout to ch3.Tin.
items.problem_signature: A temperature measurement is of order 1e9, or a FuelPin.Q_fission input is driven by a temperature output such as Channel.Tout.
items.recommended_strategy: Audit every PowerSource.P connection and every FuelPin.Q_fission input. Replace any power-to-temperature or temperature-to-power routing with PowerSource.P -> FuelPin.Q_fission and the appropriate temperature chain.
known_pitfalls: Adding the correct PowerSource connection without removing the wrong one can create an over-determined system, as in episode 2 step 15.
A FuelPin.Q_fission input driven by Channel.Tout can make initialization inconsistent because a temperature is being used as fission power.

items.title: Every Channel.mdot needs the same flow source
items.description: For series Channel plants, each Channel.mdot input must be driven exactly once by the flow Const output; outputs may fan out to multiple inputs. Episode 5 was under-determined when ch1.mdot was missing; replacing ch2.mdot with ch1.mdot did not fix it, and success required both connect(mdot.y, ch1.mdot) and connect(mdot.y, ch2.mdot).
items.problem_signature: Build reports too few equations/under-determined system, or inspect shows one or more Channel.mdot inputs unconnected.
items.recommended_strategy: Count all input connectors from the port table, then add one connection from the flow Const.y to each Channel.mdot. Do not move an existing mdot connection from one channel to another when the requirement is every input driven exactly once.
known_pitfalls: Replacing one mdot connection with another leaves the same number of equations and does not repair an under-determined model.
Adding a second driver to an already-driven input can over-determine the model.

items.title: Self-driven Sensor creates circular equalities
items.description: In a sensor_loop plant, connect(sens.y, sens.y_in) is a self-feedback loop that can produce circular equalities during index reduction. Episode 1 failed with circular equalities while sens.y drove both sens.y_in and sg.Tin; the agent then misdiagnosed the Channel/FuelPin thermal feedback and left duplicate fp.Tcool drivers, causing structural failure.
items.problem_signature: Build fails with Pantelides/index-reduction circular equalities in a loop containing Sensor.y -> Sensor.y_in.
items.recommended_strategy: When circular equalities appear, inspect the loop for a Sensor output driving its own input. Repair the physical loop first by identifying the intended measured hot-leg temperature source and the cold-leg return path; do not randomly replace Channel.Tavg -> FuelPin.Tcool.
known_pitfalls: Do not replace a valid Channel.Tavg -> FuelPin.Tcool connection with Channel.Tin -> FuelPin.Tcool; both ports are inputs and the tool will reject or leave the input unconnected.
Do not add a second connection to fp.Tcool while the original remains; this creates over-determination.

items.title: Duplicate input drivers over-determine the model
items.description: Adding a correct connection without removing the wrong connection can make the model over-determined even when all inputs appear connected. Episode 1 added ch.Tout -> fp.Tcool while ch.Tin -> fp.Tcool remained, producing too many equations; episode 2 added ps2.P -> fp2.Q_fission before removing ps2.P -> ch3.Tin, also producing too many equations.
items.problem_signature: Build fails with too many equations/over-determined system immediately after add_connect, or final model has two connect statements ending at the same input.
items.recommended_strategy: Use replace_connect when changing the source of an already-driven input. If add_connect is used, first remove the wrong connection to that same input, then run_simulation and inspect the final equation list.
known_pitfalls: The tool may report 'All inputs connected' even when an input is multiply driven.
Calling replace_connect with an old pair that no longer exists fails; re-read the model before replacing.

items.title: Channel Q_fuel needs FuelPin Qcool
items.description: In series or parallel Channel/FuelPin thermal-hydraulic plants, a Channel.Q_fuel input must be driven by the corresponding FuelPin.Qcool output, not by a PowerSource, Channel temperature output, or another input. This closes the fuel-to-coolant energy path; using a temperature or fission power signal can still compile or hit targets in some checks but violates structural conservation and off-design energy balance. Episode 1 and the successful repair in episode 4 used this routing with all conservation checks passing, while episode 2 left ch1.Q_fuel effectively unconnected and episode 3 used an input as a source.
items.problem_signature: Channel.Q_fuel driven by PowerSource.P, Channel.Tout/Tavg, FuelPin.Q_fission, or left unconnected; verifier reports unconnected ch*.Q_fuel or structural_ok=false despite goal_ok=true.
items.recommended_strategy: For each Channel, identify its paired FuelPin and connect that FuelPin.Qcool output to the Channel.Q_fuel input. Then verify every Channel.Q_fuel has exactly one incoming connection and that no input port appears on the left side of connect(...).
known_pitfalls: Do not connect PowerSource.P directly to Channel.Q_fuel; PowerSource.P belongs to FuelPin.Q_fission.
Do not use Channel.Tout or Channel.Tavg as heat input; those are temperature signals, not heat flow.
Do not connect FuelPin.Q_fission to Channel.Q_fuel; Q_fission is an input, not an output.

items.title: Series coolant inlet uses upstream Tout
items.description: In a two-Channel series plant, the downstream Channel.Tin input must be driven by the upstream Channel.Tout output. The inlet Const drives only the first Channel.Tin; using FuelPin.Qcool or another heat-flow output as a temperature inlet produces absurd temperatures and failed bounds checks. Episode 1 assembled this path successfully, and episode 2's initial T2 = 3.4e+09 was repaired to a physical value by replacing fp1.Qcool -> ch2.Tin with ch1.Tout -> ch2.Tin.
items.problem_signature: Downstream Channel.Tin is driven by a heat-flow output or by the inlet Const; simulation shows T2 of order 1e9 or downstream temperatures far outside bounds.
items.recommended_strategy: Order the Channels by coolant path, connect the inlet Const.y to the first Channel.Tin, then connect each upstream Channel.Tout to the next Channel.Tin. Check that temperature inputs receive temperature outputs and heat inputs receive heat outputs.
known_pitfalls: Do not fan out the inlet Const to every Channel.Tin in a series plant; that bypasses upstream heating.
Do not use FuelPin.Qcool as a temperature boundary; it is a heat-flow output.

items.title: Goal match can hide structural failure
items.description: In these assembly/repair tasks, run_simulation and compare_to_targets can report exact design-point agreement even when the verifier later marks structural_ok=false because an input connector is not driven exactly once or a connection is duplicated. Episodes 3 and 5 both hit all targets but failed due to structural defects: an input-as-source connection to ch1.Q_fuel and a duplicated fp2.Qcool -> ch2.Q_fuel connection. Treat target agreement as necessary but not sufficient; structural checks must be satisfied independently.
items.problem_signature: compare_to_targets all OK and physics_ok true, but verifier structural_ok=false, unconnected_inputs nonempty, or final model contains duplicate connect(...) statements.
items.recommended_strategy: Before submit, enumerate all declared input ports and count incoming connect(...) statements: exactly one per input, from an output port of compatible physical meaning. Remove duplicate connections even if simulation still succeeds, and do not accept a connection whose source is listed as an input in the port table.
known_pitfalls: A duplicate connection can make the equation system over-determined or can be silently tolerated by the simulator while still failing structural verification.
An input port used as a source may leave the real target input unconnected even when the tool reports all inputs connected after a later edit.

items.title: Input ports cannot be connection sources
items.description: When completing or repairing connect(...) statements, the left-hand side must be an output port from the component port table. Episodes 3 and 6 show repeated tool errors from trying to connect Channel.Q_fuel, FuelPin.Q_fission, Mixer.m1/m2, or Channel.mdot as sources; these are inputs. This is a tool/format and structural error class, not a physics or tuning issue, and it often leaves the intended target input unconnected.
items.problem_signature: Tool rejects 'both are inputs; a connection must go output -> input', or final model has connect(<input>, <input>) while verifier reports unconnected_inputs.
items.recommended_strategy: Build a source list from the outputs column only. For each unconnected input, choose a source output with the same physical quantity: temperature outputs for temperature inputs, mass-flow outputs for mass-flow inputs, heat-flow outputs for heat-flow inputs, and PowerSource.P only for FuelPin.Q_fission.
known_pitfalls: Do not use an instance name such as mdot as a port; use mdot.y.
Do not reverse a valid connection to satisfy an unconnected-input report; direction is output -> input.

items.title: Canonical two-stage series wiring procedure
items.description: For two-Channel/two-FuelPin series assembly tasks, a demonstrably successful procedure is to wire boundary conditions first, then coolant series path, then fuel-to-coolant heat and thermal feedback loops. Episode 1 assembled all ten inputs in this pattern and passed simulation, physics, target comparison, and verifier checks; episode 4's successful repair converged to the same structural pattern after correcting ch2.Q_fuel.
items.problem_signature: Two FuelPin/Channel pairs with Const mdot, Const tin, and two PowerSources; ten input connectors must be driven exactly once.
items.recommended_strategy: Connect mdot.y to both Channel.mdot inputs, tin.y to the first Channel.Tin, first Channel.Tout to second Channel.Tin, each PowerSource.P to its FuelPin.Q_fission, each FuelPin.Qcool to its Channel.Q_fuel, and each Channel.Tavg to its FuelPin.Tcool. Then run simulation, check physics, compare targets, and inspect structural driver counts before submit.
known_pitfalls: Do not replace FuelPin.Qcool -> Channel.Q_fuel with PowerSource.P -> Channel.Q_fuel even if a target comparison improves.
Do not leave a duplicate connection after a repair; every input must be driven exactly once.

items.title: Input ports cannot be connection sources
items.description: When adding or replacing connect(...) statements, the left-hand side must be an output port from the component port table; input-to-input and output-to-output pairs are rejected or create invalid equations. Episodes 4, 5, and 6 repeatedly attempted pairs such as fp.Tcool->ch.Tin, fp.Q_fission->ch.Q_fuel, ch.Q_fuel->split.m, and ch3.Tout->mix.T, causing tool/format errors and stalled assembly. This is a tool/format and structural error class, not a physics imbalance.
items.problem_signature: Tool reports 'both are inputs', 'both are outputs', 'has no port', duplicate connection, or no valid connections added.
items.recommended_strategy: Before each add_connect/replace_connect, classify both endpoints from the port table as output or input. Only submit output->input pairs; use outputs such as Const.y, PowerSource.P, FuelPin.Qcool, Channel.Tout/Tavg, Splitter.T1/m1/T2/m2, Mixer.T/m, and SteamGenerator.Tout/Qsg as sources. If a desired signal is an input, find the upstream component output that produces it instead of connecting the input directly.
known_pitfalls: Do not use FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Tcool, Channel.Tin, Channel.mdot, Channel.Q_fuel, Splitter.T, Splitter.m, Mixer.T1/m1/T2/m2, or SteamGenerator.Tin/mdot as sources.
Do not use Mixer.T/m or Channel.Tout/Tavg as targets.
Repeatedly resubmitting the same invalid pair wastes steps; the port direction will not change.

items.title: Duplicate connections violate exactly-once inputs
items.description: These tasks require every input connector to be driven exactly once; adding the same connection twice or replacing a connection with another that leaves the same input multiply driven creates structural failure even if the simulator builds. Episodes 3, 4, 5, and 6 show duplicate fp.Qcool->ch.Q_fuel, duplicate ps.P->fp.Q_fission, and multiple sources to ch3.mdot/ch3.Q_fuel. This is a structural error class distinct from tool syntax errors and from physical conservation failures.
items.problem_signature: Tool reports 'duplicate', final model has repeated connect(...) lines, or verifier reports structural_ok=false/unconnected_inputs despite apparent connections.
items.recommended_strategy: Maintain a one-row-per-input connection ledger. Before adding a connection, check whether the target input already has a source; before replacing, remove or overwrite the old source so the target has exactly one driver. After edits, read the final model and count each input connector once, including inputs hidden by malformed edit strings.
known_pitfalls: Outputs may fan out, but inputs may not be multiply driven.
A replace_connect that swaps in an input-as-source can leave the original target unconnected while adding an invalid equation.
Large edit_file replacements can accidentally duplicate earlier connect lines, as in episode 3.

items.title: Splitter/Mixer mass ports must follow topology
items.description: In parallel3 plants, Splitter.m1/m2 outputs are the mass-flow sources for downstream Channel.mdot and Mixer.m1/m2 inputs; Mixer.m is an output, not an input, and Channel.Q_fuel is an input, not a mass source. Episode 1 had mmix 10% low and T3/Tf3 off because ch3.mdot was driven by split1.m1 instead of the downstream split2 branch; the attempted repair to split2.m1 still left mix1/mix2 mass routing inconsistent and goal_ok=false. Episode 6 failed structurally by connecting Mixer.m to Channel.mdot/Q_fuel and Channel.Q_fuel to Splitter.m.
items.problem_signature: mmix or branch outlet temperatures off while Tin and total mdot are OK; mass-flow inputs connected from wrong splitter branch, mixer output, or heat input port.
items.recommended_strategy: Trace the hydraulic tree from Const.mdot into Splitter.m, then from each Splitter.m1/m2 to the corresponding Channel.mdot and downstream Mixer.m1/m2. Use Splitter.T1/T2 for temperature routing and Mixer.T/m only as outputs to downstream temperature/mass targets. Check that each branch Channel.mdot source matches the same splitter branch that supplies its Tin and that mixer mass inputs sum to the design mmix.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect Mixer.m to Channel.mdot or Channel.Q_fuel; Mixer.m is an output.
Do not connect Channel.Q_fuel to Splitter.m; both are inputs and Q_fuel is heat, not mass flow.
Do not use an upstream splitter branch for a downstream channel if a second splitter defines that branch flow.

items.title: Repair by port-table ledger, then verify
items.description: For assembly/repair tasks, first build a ledger of all input ports and required output drivers from the component port table, then add only output->input connections, then run simulation, check_physics, and compare_to_targets before submitting. Episode 2 demonstrates the successful minimal version: identify the single unconnected FuelPin.Tcool input, add ch2.Tavg->fp2.Tcool, then verify simulation, physics, and targets. Episodes 3-6 show that skipping the ledger and making broad edits leads to duplicate connections, unconnected inputs, and corrupted topology.
items.problem_signature: Build under-determined, unconnected inputs, repeated invalid add_connect calls, or final model with malformed/duplicated connect lines.
items.recommended_strategy: Use a deterministic sequence: read model, inspect port table/unconnected inputs, enumerate every input exactly once, add canonical connections in small batches, read back the final model, run simulation, check physics, compare targets, and only then submit. If a broad edit_file replacement is used, immediately read_file to confirm no connect lines were duplicated or truncated.
known_pitfalls: Do not submit after only compare_to_targets if check_physics or structural verification has not been confirmed.
Do not use diagnose labels outside the allowed set; that is a tool/format error, not a diagnosis.
Do not rely on a single edit_file replacement without reading back the resulting equation section.

items.title: FuelPin fission heat comes from PowerSource.P
items.description: In loop, series, and parallel FuelPin/Channel plants, a FuelPin.Q_fission input must be driven by a PowerSource.P output. A Const.y flow signal is not a heat source; using it makes Qfuel/Qsg collapse to the flow magnitude and temperatures settle near the secondary sink, as seen in Episode 5. This is inferred from the port table and energy conservation: Q_fission is the heat input to the fuel pin, while mdot is a mass-flow boundary.
items.problem_signature: Qfuel or Qsg equals mdot instead of gigawatt-scale heat; all temperatures near Tsec or inlet; fp.Q_fission driven by mdot.y.
items.recommended_strategy: Before simulating, audit each FuelPin.Q_fission connection. Replace any non-PowerSource driver with the corresponding PowerSource.P output, then re-run simulation, physics, and target comparison.
known_pitfalls: Do not use Const.y as a generic filler just because it is an available output.
Do not treat a structurally connected model as physically meaningful when heat and flow signal types are swapped.

items.title: FuelPin.Tcool sees Channel.Tavg, not Tout
items.description: For FuelPin/Channel pairs, the FuelPin.Tcool input must be driven by the corresponding Channel.Tavg output. Channel.Tout is the downstream bulk outlet temperature used for series routing, splitters, mixers, or steam-generator inlet, not the average coolant temperature seen by the pin. Episode 5 showed that replacing Channel.Tavg with Channel.Tout did not fix the heat-source fault, while successful series and parallel models consistently used Channel.Tavg for FuelPin.Tcool.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin.Tcool connected to Channel.Tout, Channel.Tin, or another temperature input; fuel/clad temperatures off while channel outlet routing otherwise looks plausible.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin/Channel pair, verify the local thermal feedback triangle: PowerSource.P to FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Qcool to Channel.Q_fuel, and Channel.Tavg to FuelPin.Tcool. Keep Channel.Tout for hydraulic downstream temperature propagation only.
known_pitfalls: Do not confuse Channel.Tavg with Channel.Tout when diagnosing a wrong_routing label.
Do not use Channel.Tin as FuelPin.Tcool; it is an input and also not the average coolant temperature.

items.title: Loop cold leg is SteamGenerator.Tout to Channel.Tin
items.description: In a recirculating loop with Channel and SteamGenerator, the Channel.Tin input must be driven by SteamGenerator.Tout, while SteamGenerator.Tin is driven by Channel.Tout. This closes the thermal-hydraulic loop: the channel outlet is the hot-leg inlet to the heat sink, and the steam-generator outlet is the cold-leg inlet to the channel. Episode 1 failed structurally by trying to drive SteamGenerator.Tin from FuelPin.Qcool and by attempting input-to-input temperature connections.
items.problem_signature: Loop assembly has unconnected Channel.Tin or SteamGenerator.Tin; attempts to connect FuelPin.Tcool, Channel.Tin, or SteamGenerator.Tin as sources; heat output connected to a temperature input.
items.recommended_strategy: Build the loop in two independent chains: heat chain PowerSource.P to FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Qcool to Channel.Q_fuel, Channel.Tavg to FuelPin.Tcool; flow/temperature chain Const.y to both mdot inputs, Channel.Tout to SteamGenerator.Tin, SteamGenerator.Tout to Channel.Tin.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect FuelPin.Qcool to SteamGenerator.Tin; heat and temperature signals are different physical quantities.
Do not connect Channel.Tin or SteamGenerator.Tin as left-hand-side sources; both are inputs.

items.title: All inputs connected does not imply correct routing
items.description: In repair and assembly tasks, a tool reporting 'All inputs connected' only verifies structural coverage, not signal type, physical conservation, or design-point correctness. Episode 5 had all inputs connected after mdot.y was wired to fp.Q_fission, but Qfuel/Qsg were 15000 instead of 3.4e9 and all temperatures were near 490 K. Episode 1 also ended with no unconnected inputs but failed build/structure because a heat output was connected to a temperature input.
items.problem_signature: Tool says all inputs connected, but simulation shows heat equal to flow, temperatures pinned to sink/inlet, physics failures, or build/structural failure.
items.recommended_strategy: After every structural completion, run a three-stage check: inspect port directions and signal meanings, run_simulation plus check_physics, then compare_to_targets. If physics passes but goals fail, suspect wrong routing or wrong boundary condition rather than missing connections.
known_pitfalls: Do not submit immediately after 'All inputs connected'.
Do not use a generic wrong_routing diagnosis as evidence that a specific replacement is correct.

items.title: Repair missing connections by port-type audit
items.description: For series and parallel repair tasks with one missing connection, a port-table audit followed by a single typed add_connect can restore the design point. Episodes 3 and 4 succeeded by adding the missing Channel.mdot or Channel.Tin driver, then verifying simulation, physics, and targets. This procedure works when the existing model already has the correct local FuelPin/Channel feedback and only one input is unconnected.
items.problem_signature: Compiles or nearly compiles; inspect shows one unconnected input; other connections follow expected local feedback and routing patterns.
items.recommended_strategy: List unconnected inputs, classify each by physical quantity and direction, choose the unique output with matching quantity, add only that connection, then run simulation, physics, and target comparison before submitting.
known_pitfalls: Do not add a connection merely because the left side is an output; match heat, temperature, and mass-flow quantities.
Do not apply this single-connection procedure when physics failures indicate multiple independent faults.

items.title: FuelPin Tcool must see Channel.Tavg
items.description: In single, loop, and parallel Channel/FuelPin plants, a FuelPin.Tcool input must be driven by the corresponding Channel.Tavg output. Episode 4 succeeded only after replacing a self-connected FuelPin.Tc with Channel.Tavg; episodes 2 and 6 show that using Channel.Tout or leaving Tcool unconnected gives wrong fuel temperatures or missing inputs. This is inferred from the port table and the successful simulated design point, where coolant heat removal must use the channel average temperature rather than outlet or clad temperature.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin.Tcool driven by FuelPin.Tc, Channel.Tout, or absent; Tf/Tc grossly high while Qfuel and coolant temperatures may be plausible.
items.recommended_strategy: Inspect the exact source of every FuelPin.Tcool input; replace any non-Channel.Tavg source with the matching Channel.Tavg, and remove any duplicate connection to the same input before simulating.
known_pitfalls: Adding Channel.Tavg without removing the old Tcool connection creates an over-determined model.
Channel.Tout is not a substitute for Channel.Tavg for FuelPin.Tcool.

items.title: Duplicate input drivers overdetermine Modelica plants
items.description: When every input connector must be driven exactly once, adding a second connection to an already-driven input creates too many equations even if inspect reports no unconnected inputs. Episodes 1, 3, and 4 show duplicate Tcool or Q_fission drivers leading to BUILD FAILED or structural_ok=false; episode 4 recovered by removing the old self-connection after adding the correct one. This is a structural/tool-format error, not a physical imbalance or goal miss.
items.problem_signature: BUILD FAILED with 'Too many equations, over-determined system' after add_connect, or final model contains the same connect statement twice.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding a replacement connection, identify and remove the existing driver of that input; use replace_connect when available, and re-read the final equation list to ensure no duplicate connect remains.
known_pitfalls: inspect reporting 'Unconnected inputs: none' does not prove inputs are driven exactly once.
No-op edit_file calls can leave duplicate connections hidden in the final model.

items.title: SteamGenerator Tin needs Channel.Tout in loop
items.description: In loop plants with Channel and SteamGenerator in series, SteamGenerator.Tin must be driven by Channel.Tout, while SteamGenerator.Tout drives Channel.Tin. Episode 6 replaced Channel.Tout with Channel.Tavg for SteamGenerator.Tin and produced Qsg half of Qfuel and all temperatures low; the original loop wiring with Channel.Tout is consistent with hot-leg heat removal. This is inferred from the port table, energy balance, and the observed Qsg/Qfuel mismatch after the replacement.
items.problem_signature: Loop plant has Qfuel at target but Qsg about half target and hot/cold leg temperatures shifted low after SG.Tin is driven by Channel.Tavg.
items.recommended_strategy: For loop heat removal, verify the hot-leg connection Channel.Tout -> SteamGenerator.Tin and the cold-leg return SteamGenerator.Tout -> Channel.Tin; do not use Channel.Tavg as the SG inlet.
known_pitfalls: Channel.Tavg is appropriate for FuelPin.Tcool but not for SteamGenerator.Tin.
A structurally valid loop can still miss the design point if the SG inlet uses the wrong temperature port.

items.title: High Tf with balanced Q is parameter fault
items.description: In tuning or multistep tasks, if Qfuel, mdot, Tin, Tout/Tavg, and clad temperature are near target but fuel centerline temperature Tf is thousands of kelvin high, the fault is a FuelPin conductance parameter such as G_gap or G_cl, not a routing fault. Episodes 1 and 2 show this signature with G_gap=1000000 or G_cl changes; episode 5 shows low Qfuel with all temperatures low indicating PowerSource.P0, not routing. Treating these as wrong_routing led to duplicate connections or irrelevant rewiring.
items.problem_signature: compare_to_targets shows only Tf grossly OFF while Tc, Qfuel, mdot, and coolant temperatures are OK; or Qfuel and all temperatures scale low together with P0 low.
items.recommended_strategy: First classify by measured pattern: use parameter tuning for isolated Tf/Tc offsets or global heat-input offsets; only edit connections when inspect shows missing, duplicate, or wrong port drivers. For isolated high Tf, adjust FuelPin G_gap/G_cl; for low Qfuel and low temperatures, adjust PowerSource.P0.
action_template: if isolated_Tf_error: set_parameter(<fuelpin>, G_gap or G_cl, <candidate>)
known_pitfalls: Do not record diagnose('wrong_routing') when all inputs are connected exactly once and conservation checks pass.
Setting a parameter to its current value is a no-op; verify the numeric value actually changes.

items.title: Repair connections by exact driver replacement
items.description: For repair tasks with a compiling but off-design plant, a successful procedure is to read the model, inspect port drivers, simulate and compare, then replace the exact wrong connection while preserving one driver per input. Episode 4 demonstrates the working sequence: add the correct Channel.Tavg -> FuelPin.Tcool, remove the old FuelPin.Tc -> FuelPin.Tcool, simulate, compare, and submit. Episodes 3 and 6 show that adding without removing, or replacing a correct hot-leg connection, causes overdetermination or a goal miss.
items.problem_signature: Compiling model with all inputs connected but one wrong source port; inspect shows no unconnected inputs, so the fault is hidden in connection semantics.
items.recommended_strategy: Use the port table to map each input to its required source type and port; perform a single exact replacement or remove-then-add; rerun simulation and compare before any further edits.
known_pitfalls: replace_connect with identical old and new does nothing.
Attempting to replace a connection that does not exist exactly once fails; inspect the current model first.
Do not submit after a simulation that still misses design targets.

items.title: FuelPin Tcool uses paired Channel Tavg
items.description: In Channel/FuelPin assemblies, each FuelPin.Tcool input must be driven by the Tavg output of the Channel receiving that same FuelPin.Qcool heat. Episode 2 shows crossed Tavg links can leave bulk temperatures and mass/energy checks apparently acceptable while only fuel temperatures miss targets; replacing each crossed link with the paired Channel.Tavg restores the design point. This is a structural feedback rule, not a tuning rule.
items.problem_signature: All inputs connected and conservation passes, but Tf/Tc targets are selectively wrong while channel outlet/mixed temperatures are correct.
items.recommended_strategy: For every FuelPin, trace Qcool to its Channel.Q_fuel, then verify that same Channel.Tavg drives that FuelPin.Tcool; repair crossed or foreign Tavg links before changing parameters.
known_pitfalls: Do not use Channel.Tout for FuelPin.Tcool in these models; the successful episodes use Channel.Tavg.
Do not treat a crossed Tcool link as a parameter error just because physics checks pass.

items.title: Never satisfy unconnected inputs with wrong-type outputs
items.description: In assembly tasks with Splitter/Mixer/Channel components, a tool may accept a connection if it is output-to-input even when the physical quantity is wrong, such as Channel.Tout or Mixer.T driving a mass input. Episode 4 reaches 'All inputs connected' but fails build because temperature outputs were connected to Mixer.m1/m2 and Splitter.T, and Mixer outputs were connected back into Splitter inputs. Structural validity requires both port direction and physical port role: temperature outputs drive temperature inputs, mass-flow outputs drive mass-flow inputs, heat outputs drive heat inputs.
items.problem_signature: Repeated add_connect errors mention nonexistent ports, input-to-input connections, or duplicates; later 'All inputs connected' is followed by build failure or under-determined/nonphysical equations.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding connections, enumerate each input by physical role. Use Const.y for boundary Tin/mdot, Splitter.T1/T2 for Channel.Tin, Splitter.m1/m2 for Channel.mdot and Mixer.m1/m2, Channel.Tout for Mixer.T1/T2, FuelPin.Qcool for Channel.Q_fuel, and PowerSource.P for FuelPin.Q_fission. Re-read the model after partial additions to avoid duplicate calls.
known_pitfalls: Channel has no mout output; do not invent one for Mixer mass inputs.
Channel.Q_fuel is an input, not a source for Mixer.m or Splitter.m.
Mixer.T and Mixer.m are outputs; connecting them to Splitter.T/Splitter.m reverses the intended flow path.

items.title: Do not tune conductances when heat input is low
items.description: In tuning tasks with multiple FuelPin/Channel branches, if all branch outlet temperatures and fuel temperatures are low together while Tin and mdot are on target, changing FuelPin G_cl mainly changes fuel-to-clad temperature drop and has little effect on coolant heating. Episode 6 repeatedly changed G_cl values while Tmix, T1, T2, and T3 stayed unchanged and Qfuel remained governed by PowerSource.P0; the design point stayed missed. Check global heat source and flow split before local heat-transfer coefficients when coolant temperature rise is too small.
items.problem_signature: Tmix and all branch outlet temperatures are below target by similar relative amounts, fuel temperatures are far below target, Tin/mdot are OK, and G_cl edits leave Tmix/T1/T2/T3 unchanged.
items.recommended_strategy: First compare Qfuel/PowerSource.P0 and mdot/Tin to the design point; if coolant enthalpy rise is too low, adjust the heat-source parameter or boundary/flow parameter indicated by the target comparison. Only tune G_gap/G_cl when coolant temperatures are already near target but Tf/Tc residuals indicate a local conductance issue.
known_pitfalls: Do not infer a correct PowerSource.P0 value from these trajectories; Episode 6 does not demonstrate a successful power adjustment.
Do not use G_cl edits to raise coolant outlet temperature when Qfuel is unchanged.

items.title: Tune mdot when only flow is off
items.description: For a single Channel/FuelPin plant with correct topology, if Qfuel and Tin are on target but Tout, Tavg, Tf, and Tc are all high while mdot is below target, setting the Const.mdot parameter to the design flow can restore all thermal targets. Episode 1 demonstrates this: changing mdot.k from 3600 to 15000 made Tout, Tavg, Tf, and Tc match exactly while Qfuel and Tin stayed unchanged, with steady state and conservation checks passing. This applies to parameter tuning, not to structural faults.
items.problem_signature: All connections are valid, Qfuel and Tin match targets, mdot is off target, and all coolant/fuel temperatures are biased in the direction expected from too-low or too-high flow.
items.recommended_strategy: When the only off-spec boundary parameter is the flow Const, set its k to the target mdot, then rerun simulation, compare all targets, and check physics before submitting.
known_pitfalls: Do not apply this when structural_ok is false or when Qsg/Qfuel imbalance indicates wrong SteamGenerator routing.
Do not change FuelPin conductances if the flow boundary itself is explicitly off target.

items.title: FuelPin Tcool must see Channel.Tavg
items.description: In single- and series-channel plants with FuelPin and Channel components, a FuelPin.Tcool input must be driven by the paired Channel.Tavg output, not by a Const inlet temperature or Channel.Tin. The FuelPin heat removal depends on the coolant temperature in the heated channel; using Tin underpredicts the coolant temperature seen by the pin and shifts Tf/Tc/Qcool. This does not apply to plants whose library explicitly defines a different coolant-temperature input semantics.
items.problem_signature: All inputs connected and conservation passes, but fuel/clad temperatures and downstream temperatures are off while Tin and mdot are correct.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin, identify its heat-removal Channel and connect that Channel.Tavg output to the FuelPin.Tcool input; reject any Const.y->FuelPin.Tcool or Channel.Tin->FuelPin.Tcool wiring.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect two inputs together, e.g. <fuelpin>.Tcool -> <channel>.Tin.
Do not use <channel>.Tin as a source; it is an input.

items.title: Series Channel inlet uses upstream Tout
items.description: For two Channel components in a coolant series path, the downstream Channel.Tin input must be driven by the upstream Channel.Tout output. Driving it from the inlet Const or from a FuelPin.Tc output breaks the series energy path: the second channel does not receive the upstream coolant enthalpy rise, so downstream Tout/Tavg and fuel temperatures miss the design point. This does not apply to parallel-channel designs where each Channel.Tin is intentionally driven by the common inlet boundary.
items.problem_signature: First-stage temperatures match, but second-stage T2/Tf2 are low or high while Tin, mdot, and first-stage outputs are correct.
items.recommended_strategy: Check the coolant path order and connect upstream Channel.Tout to downstream Channel.Tin; use the inlet Const only on the first Channel.Tin in a series plant.
known_pitfalls: FuelPin.Tc is a clad temperature output, not a coolant outlet temperature.
A Const inlet may fan out to multiple Channel.Tin only for parallel topology, not series.

items.title: FuelPin fission heat comes from PowerSource
items.description: In FuelPin/Channel plants, FuelPin.Q_fission must be driven by a PowerSource.P output, while FuelPin.Qcool drives Channel.Q_fuel. Connecting FuelPin.Qcool back into FuelPin.Q_fission creates a self-driven heat input that can still compile and pass component conservation but changes Qfuel and all temperatures. This does not apply if a task explicitly defines a different external fission-power source component type.
items.problem_signature: Qfuel is far from the specified PowerSource value and Tout/Tavg/Tf/Tc are shifted, while Tin and mdot are correct.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin, connect the corresponding PowerSource.P to FuelPin.Q_fission and connect FuelPin.Qcool only to the paired Channel.Q_fuel; remove any Qcool->Q_fission feedback connection.
known_pitfalls: Do not treat Qcool as the fission source; it is the heat delivered to coolant.
Adding the correct source before removing the wrong one may temporarily violate exactly-once input driving.

items.title: All inputs connected is not enough
items.description: In assembly/repair tasks, a model can have every input driven exactly once, compile, simulate, and pass conservation checks while still failing the design point because the drivers are structurally wrong. Episode 2 shows that duplicate-safe add_connect calls and an 'All inputs connected' message do not validate physical routing; compare_to_targets exposed the goal error. This failure class is structural/goal, not a tool/format error, and does not apply when target mismatches are caused by parameter values or boundary constants.
items.problem_signature: Verifier or tool reports no unconnected inputs and physics passes, but compare_to_targets shows several temperature or heat-flow targets off.
items.recommended_strategy: After connectivity is complete, audit each input against its required source type and topology role, then run simulation, compare_to_targets, and check_physics before submit.
known_pitfalls: Do not submit immediately after 'All inputs connected'.
Do not confuse duplicate add_connect rejections with successful structural validation.

items.title: Repair wrong routing by exact current text
items.description: For repair tasks where a wrong connection is present, first read the current model text and use the exact connect(...) string in edit_file or replace_connect. Episode 4 succeeded by replacing connect(fp1.Tc, ch2.Tin) with connect(ch1.Tout, ch2.Tin); Episode 2 repeatedly failed edit_file because it guessed old strings that did not occur exactly once. This procedure is for structural rewiring, not for parameter tuning or missing-connection-only assembly.
items.problem_signature: A known wrong connect exists, but replace_connect or edit_file reports 'not found exactly once' or 'old string occurs 0 times'.
items.recommended_strategy: Read the file immediately before editing, copy the exact current connection line, replace only that line with the output->input connection required by the port table, then rerun simulation and target comparison.
known_pitfalls: Do not use a remembered or hypothesized connection string after failed add_connect calls.
Do not omit the old argument to edit_file; the tool requires an exact old string.

items.title: FuelPin Tcool must see Channel Tavg
items.description: In loop and parallel Channel/FuelPin plants, a FuelPin.Tcool input must be driven by the corresponding Channel.Tavg output, not by a Const flow value, Channel.Tin, or another input port. This follows from the port table and thermal coupling: Tcool is a coolant temperature state used by FuelPin heat transfer, while mdot is a mass-flow input. Driving Tcool with mdot can leave hydraulic targets correct but produce physically impossible fuel/clad temperatures, as in Ep1 where Tf/Tc became ~1.7e4 while Thot/Tcold/Qsg/Qfuel matched.
items.problem_signature: All hydraulic/loop temperatures and powers meet targets, but FuelPin Tf/Tc are extremely high or off-target; check_physics reports bounds:temperature while component energy residuals are small.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin, verify that Q_fission is driven by PowerSource.P, Qcool drives the paired Channel.Q_fuel, and Tcool is driven by that same Channel.Tavg. Do not use Const.mdot.y or any input port as a temperature source.
known_pitfalls: Using mdot.y to fill an unconnected Tcool input because it is an available output.
Assuming Channel.Tin is the correct coolant temperature for FuelPin.Tcool; Channel.Tin is an input and not the average coolant temperature.
Treating a passing compare_to_targets for Thot/Tcold/Qfuel as proof that fuel temperatures are physically valid.

items.title: No-op parameter edits do not tune
items.description: In tuning tasks, repeatedly setting a parameter to its current value is a no-op and cannot repair an off-design target. Ep2 repeatedly set fp2.G_cl to 1.8e+08, which was already the initial value, while Tf2 remained 667.423 instead of 973.423; Ep3 changed mdot.k away from target and then restored it, leaving Tf2 at 2123.46. The signature is identical simulation and compare_to_targets outputs before and after set_parameter.
items.problem_signature: set_parameter reports OK but run_simulation/check_physics/compare_to_targets values are unchanged; the chosen value equals the current model value or is restored after a transient trial.
items.recommended_strategy: Before editing, read the current parameter value from the model. If the target mismatch is localized to one FuelPin temperature while all flow and mixed temperatures are correct, test a different relevant FuelPin conductance parameter with a changed value, then rerun simulation and compare_to_targets. Do not repeat the same set_parameter call.
known_pitfalls: Confusing a successful tool call with a changed model state.
Changing global mdot when only one branch fuel temperature is off and mdot/mmix/Tmix already meet targets.
Using diagnose labels not in the allowed set instead of continuing parameter search.

items.title: Wrong port direction corrupts assembly
items.description: Assembly attempts fail structurally when connect(...) uses an input port as the source, an output port as the target, or a non-existent port. Ep4 tried fp.Tcool->ch.Tin and fp.Tcool->sg.Tin, both input-to-input, then connected fp.Qcool to sg.Tin; Ep6 tried FuelPin.Tcool->Splitter.T and Channel.Tout->Splitter.T1, confusing Splitter inputs and outputs. These are tool/format and structural errors, not physics or goal errors, and can produce build failure or an under-determined model.
items.problem_signature: add_connect errors such as 'both are inputs', 'both are outputs', 'has no port', duplicate connection, or BUILD FAILED under-determined system after many connections.
items.recommended_strategy: Use the port table as a ledger: list every input connector and choose exactly one output driver from the outputs column. For Splitter/Mixer, remember Splitter has inputs T,m and outputs T1,m1,T2,m2; Mixer has inputs T1,m1,T2,m2 and outputs T,m. Re-inspect after bulk edits and replace only connections that actually exist.
known_pitfalls: Using an input port name such as FuelPin.Tcool or Splitter.T as a connection source.
Treating Splitter.T1/T2/m1/m2 as inputs; they are outputs.
Treating Mixer.T/m as inputs; they are outputs.
Adding duplicate connections after a partially successful bulk add_connect.

items.title: Missing Qcool link repair works
items.description: In a parallel2 multistep repair, the only missing connection was fp1.Qcool->ch1.Q_fuel; adding it made all inputs connected and produced exact target agreement plus all conservation checks passing. This demonstrates a reusable repair pattern: when one FuelPin/Channel branch lacks the heat-flow coupling while its Tcool feedback and hydraulic connections are already present, add the paired FuelPin.Qcool to Channel.Q_fuel link before changing parameters.
items.problem_signature: Port-table inspection shows a single unconnected Channel.Q_fuel input in an otherwise wired FuelPin/Channel branch; other branches have Qcool->Q_fuel and Tavg->Tcool.
items.recommended_strategy: Compare branches by component type. For each FuelPin/Channel pair, ensure PowerSource.P->FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Qcool->Channel.Q_fuel, and Channel.Tavg->FuelPin.Tcool. Add only the missing output->input connection, then run simulation, check_physics, and compare_to_targets before submitting.
known_pitfalls: Changing PowerSource.P or conductance parameters when a heat-flow connection is missing.
Submitting after only structural 'All inputs connected' without physics and target verification.
Applying this branch-comparison shortcut to a plant where multiple independent faults are visible.

items.title: FuelPin fission input needs PowerSource.P
items.description: In assembly or repair tasks with FuelPin and PowerSource components, every FuelPin.Q_fission input must be driven by a PowerSource.P output. Without that link, the FuelPin has no fission heat source, so Channel.Q_fuel and downstream temperatures cannot represent the intended powered branch; this is a structural missing-connection fault, not a tuning fault. It does not apply when the task intentionally uses a different heat source component or when Q_fission is already driven exactly once.
items.problem_signature: Unconnected FuelPin.Q_fission or a branch with low/absent heat while all other inputs are connected.
items.recommended_strategy: Inspect the port table, enumerate all FuelPin.Q_fission inputs, and add exactly one connect(<powersource>.P, <fuelpin>.Q_fission) for each undriven input; then run simulation, check_physics, and compare_to_targets before submitting.
known_pitfalls: Do not reverse the pair as FuelPin.Q_fission -> PowerSource.P; the port table defines output -> input direction.
Do not add a second driver to an already connected Q_fission input; every input connector must be driven exactly once.

items.title: No-op edits do not repair goal misses
items.description: In tuning tasks where build_ok, structural_ok, and physics_ok are already true but goal_ok is false, setting a parameter to its current value or replacing a connection with the identical pair changes nothing. Episodes 1 and 6 show repeated no-op set_parameter and replace_connect calls while downstream temperatures remained off target; this is a goal error, not a tool, structural, or physics error. It does not apply when the parameter value actually differs from the current model value or when the replacement pair changes a real source or target.
items.problem_signature: Simulation and physics pass, design point misses persist, and tool calls report OK for set_parameter with unchanged value or replace_connect with old == new.
items.recommended_strategy: Before editing, compare the current model value or connection pair with the proposed value or pair; if identical, do not call the edit. For a real goal miss, identify which measured quantities are off, then change a parameter that plausibly affects those quantities or repair a non-identical connection, followed by run_simulation and compare_to_targets.
known_pitfalls: Do not interpret diagnose(label=wrong_parameter) or diagnose(label=wrong_routing) as evidence that a no-op edit fixed the plant.
Do not submit or stop after a no-op edit; re-run compare_to_targets only after a substantive model change.

items.title: Duplicate connections over-determine thermal plants
items.description: In assembly tasks with Channel/FuelPin feedback loops, adding the same connect statement twice or leaving a duplicate driver on an input can make the model over-determined even if the tool reports all inputs connected. Episode 4 ended with duplicate ch2.Tavg->fp2.Tcool and ch1.Tout->ch2.Tin connections and build failed with too many equations; this is a structural error. It does not apply to legitimate fan-out from one output to multiple different inputs, which is allowed by the task requirements.
items.problem_signature: BUILD FAILED with 'Too many equations, over-determined system' after add_connect/replace_connect churn, or final model contains identical connect statements.
items.recommended_strategy: After each connection edit, read the model and count drivers per input connector; remove duplicate identical connect pairs before simulating. When replacing a connection, first remove the exact old pair, then add the new pair, and verify that no input has two drivers.
known_pitfalls: Do not use an unknown tool name such as connect; use add_connect, remove_connect, or replace_connect as available.
Do not replace a pair that is not present exactly once; first inspect the current connections.

items.title: Verify after one structural repair
items.description: For repair and multistep tasks where the only missing link is a PowerSource.P to FuelPin.Q_fission connection, a single add_connect followed by simulation, physics check, target comparison, and submit demonstrably succeeded in episodes 2 and 3. This works because the rest of the topology already conserved mass and energy and the missing fission heat input was the independent fault. It does not apply when compare_to_targets still shows off-design temperatures after the connection is added, or when physics/build checks fail.
items.problem_signature: Initial model compiles or is nearly complete, one FuelPin.Q_fission input is unconnected, and all other input connectors are driven once.
items.recommended_strategy: Add the missing PowerSource.P->FuelPin.Q_fission connection, then run the full verification chain; if all targets and conservation checks pass, submit without further parameter tuning.
known_pitfalls: Do not continue tuning parameters after all target comparisons are OK.
Do not skip check_physics when the task explicitly requires mass and energy balance.

items.title: Mixer mass inputs need Splitter mass outputs
items.description: In parallel plants with Splitter and Mixer components, Mixer.m1 and Mixer.m2 are input connectors and must be driven by mass-flow outputs, typically Splitter.m1/m2 or the corresponding branch flow outputs. Connecting only Mixer.T1/T2 leaves the model under-determined or structurally invalid even if temperature outputs are wired. This follows from the port table: Mixer inputs are T1,m1,T2,m2 and Splitter outputs include T1,m1,T2,m2.
items.problem_signature: Unconnected Mixer.m1 or Mixer.m2; under-determined system; mmix may look correct while branch temperatures are wrong.
items.recommended_strategy: Before simulating, enumerate every Mixer input and verify each has one output-to-input connection. For mass inputs, use Splitter.m1/m2 or branch mass outputs, never Channel.mdot or Mixer.m inputs.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect Mixer.m1 -> Channel.mdot; both are inputs.
Do not infer that Mixer.m output can replace missing Mixer.m1/m2 inputs.
Do not treat duplicate temperature connections as fixing missing mass-flow connections.

items.title: PowerSource.P is not a temperature signal
items.description: In repair tasks with PowerSource, FuelPin, Channel, Splitter, and Mixer, routing PowerSource.P into a temperature input such as Channel.Tin or FuelPin.Q_fission via a Splitter.T output creates physically absurd temperatures while component energy residuals may still pass. The port table and units imply PowerSource.P is a heat/power source, not a coolant temperature or branch temperature. Check for temperatures of order 1e9 and bounds:temperature failures.
items.problem_signature: Tmix, T2, Tf2, or similar temperatures near 1e9; bounds:temperature failure; PowerSource.P connected to Channel.Tin or Splitter.T1 connected to FuelPin.Q_fission.
items.recommended_strategy: Audit all PowerSource.P connections: it should drive FuelPin.Q_fission inputs only. Remove any PowerSource.P connection to temperature inputs and replace temperature inputs with Const.y, Splitter.T outputs, Channel.Tout, or Mixer.T outputs as appropriate.
known_pitfalls: Adding a missing FuelPin.Q_fission connection without removing the bad PowerSource.P-to-temperature connection can over-determine the model.
A diagnosis of wrong_routing is insufficient unless the specific bad connection is removed.
Energy residuals can pass even when temperature bounds fail due to unit-inconsistent routing.

items.title: FuelPin.Tcool needs Channel.Tavg, not Tin
items.description: In single-channel and loop plants with FuelPin and Channel, FuelPin.Tcool is an input and must be driven by a coolant-temperature output. The successful models use Channel.Tavg for this input; Channel.Tin is itself an input and cannot drive FuelPin.Tcool. This is inferred from the port table and from successful steady energy balance in Episodes 1-3.
items.problem_signature: Attempts like connect(fp.Tcool, ch.Tin) rejected as input-to-input; FuelPin.Tcool unconnected; under-determined system.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin, connect the paired Channel.Tavg output to FuelPin.Tcool. Use Channel.Tin only as a target input driven by Const.y, SteamGenerator.Tout, or Splitter.T outputs.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect FuelPin.Tcool to Channel.Tin; both are inputs.
Do not use Channel.Tout as a substitute for Channel.Tavg unless a task explicitly requires it; the demonstrated successful topology uses Tavg.
Do not connect Channel.Tout to Channel.Q_fuel; that is a temperature-to-heat-input mismatch.

items.title: Do not tune unchanged parameters
items.description: In tuning tasks where the topology is valid and physics checks pass, setting a parameter to its current value cannot change the operating point. Episode 2 repeatedly set FuelPin.G_gap and G_cl to their existing values while Tf and Tc remained off target; this is a goal error, not a structural or physics error. Use compare_to_targets to identify which measured quantities are off, then change only parameters that can affect those quantities and verify with a new simulation.
items.problem_signature: set_parameter reports OK but value equals initial value; subsequent run_simulation and compare_to_targets are numerically identical.
items.recommended_strategy: Read the initial model parameters before setting them. If a parameter is already at the proposed value, choose a different parameter or compute a new value; after each real change, rerun simulation and compare targets before further edits.
known_pitfalls: Do not diagnose missing_connection when inspect reports no unconnected inputs.
Do not use diagnose labels outside the allowed vocabulary; that is a tool/format error, not a plant fault.
Do not assume physics_ok implies goal_ok; a steady, conserving plant can still miss design temperatures.

items.title: Tune flow from target mdot first
items.description: For tune tasks with a Const driving Channel.mdot, if the measured mdot is off target while Qfuel and boundary temperatures are already on target, set that Const.k to the target mdot before changing heat-transfer or power parameters. Episodes 1 and 3 show this single change brings Tout, Tavg, Tf, Tc, and sensor hot-leg temperature to target with conservation checks passing. This refines the existing mdot tuning lesson by extending it from single plants to sensor-loop plants.
items.problem_signature: compare_to_targets shows mdot off by a large percentage; Qfuel/Qsg and Tin/Tcold boundary conditions are on target; several temperatures are off consistently.
items.recommended_strategy: Set the flow Const.k to the design mdot, rerun simulation, compare all targets, then run check_physics before submit. Only tune FuelPin conductances or SteamGenerator UA if temperatures remain off after mdot is on target.
known_pitfalls: Do not change FuelPin.G_gap or G_cl when mdot is the clearly off-target measured parameter.
Do not submit before check_physics even if compare_to_targets is all OK.
This does not apply when mdot is already on target but only fuel/clad temperatures are off.

items.title: FuelPin heat path requires both power and coolant feedback
items.description: In series or loop plants containing PowerSource, FuelPin, and Channel, each FuelPin.Q_fission input must be driven by a PowerSource.P output, and each FuelPin.Qcool output must drive the paired Channel.Q_fuel input. The FuelPin.Tcool input must see the paired Channel.Tavg output, not a flow constant or another input; this is inferred from the port table and energy conservation. Missing either heat-path link can leave the model compiling but produce grossly wrong fuel temperatures or downstream temperatures.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin temperature or downstream channel temperature far off target while Tin and mdot are correct; or an unconnected Q_fission/Q_fuel input.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin/Channel pair, check the three links: PowerSource.P -> FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Qcool -> Channel.Q_fuel, and Channel.Tavg -> FuelPin.Tcool. Do not connect mdot.y to FuelPin.Tcool or Channel.Tavg to Channel.mdot.
known_pitfalls: Treating a temperature output as a mass-flow driver.
Driving FuelPin.Tcool from a Const.mdot output.
Assuming a missing fission source is a parameter or boundary-condition error.

items.title: Series channels use Tout-to-Tin, not Tin fanout
items.description: In a three-Channel series plant, the coolant temperature routing is Const.tin.y -> first Channel.Tin, first Channel.Tout -> second Channel.Tin, and second Channel.Tout -> third Channel.Tin. Driving multiple Channel.Tin inputs from the same inlet constant breaks the cumulative enthalpy rise; the first stage may match while later outlet temperatures are shifted low. This is inferred from series energy balance and is supported by episode 6, where tin.y -> ch2.Tin produced T2/T3 below target.
items.problem_signature: First channel outlet matches target but second and third channel outlet temperatures are too low by roughly one or more stage temperature rises.
items.recommended_strategy: Use a port ledger to ensure only the first Channel.Tin is driven by the inlet Const; connect each upstream Channel.Tout to the next Channel.Tin. Preserve exactly one driver per input when replacing a wrong routing.
known_pitfalls: Adding the correct ch1.Tout->ch2.Tin link without removing the wrong tin.y->ch2.Tin link, causing over-determination.
Replacing ch2.Tout->ch3.Tin with ch1.Tout->ch2.Tin and leaving ch3.Tin unconnected.

items.title: Input-to-input connects leave loop underdetermined
items.description: In loop assembly tasks with FuelPin, Channel, and SteamGenerator, attempts such as FuelPin.Tcool -> Channel.Tin or Channel.Tin -> FuelPin.Tcool are invalid because both are input ports. The simulator rejects these pairs; if forced into the file, the model remains underdetermined with unconnected inputs. The correct thermal feedback source is an output such as Channel.Tavg, while the loop closure temperature source is SteamGenerator.Tout to Channel.Tin by inference from recirculating-flow energy balance.
items.problem_signature: add_connect reports 'both are inputs'; run_simulation reports too few equations; inspect still lists fp.Tcool and ch.Tin unconnected.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding connections, classify every port as input or output from the port table. Never connect two inputs; use Channel.Tavg for FuelPin.Tcool and an available temperature output for Channel.Tin. Also drive Channel.mdot and SteamGenerator.mdot from Const.y, not from Channel.Tavg.
known_pitfalls: Using Channel.Tavg as a mass-flow input to SteamGenerator.mdot.
Repeatedly retrying the same input-input pair after rejection.
Assuming 'all inputs connected' from a partial add_connect means the topology is physically correct.

items.title: Repair missing links by ledger and verification
items.description: For diagnosis/repair tasks, first inspect the port table and enumerate all input connectors with their required output drivers. Add or replace only output->input connections, then run simulation, check physics, and compare targets before submitting. Episodes 2 and 4 demonstrate that a single missing PowerSource.P->FuelPin.Q_fission or FuelPin.Qcool->Channel.Q_fuel link can be repaired this way and verified by exact target match and conservation pass.
items.problem_signature: A plant compiles or nearly compiles but has one unconnected input, a wrong routing, or off-design temperatures with conservation otherwise steady.
items.recommended_strategy: Use diagnose only with an allowed label when required; then use add_connect/replace_connect/remove_connect at port level. After each structural change, rerun simulation and physics; do not submit after no-op edits or repeated identical diagnostics.
known_pitfalls: Calling diagnose with an unsupported label.
Applying an edit whose old and new strings are identical.
Recording multiple diagnoses instead of repairing the structural fault.
Adding a correct link without removing the conflicting wrong link.

items.title: FuelPin Tcool sees paired Channel.Tavg
items.description: For a FuelPin thermally coupled to its own Channel, FuelPin.Tcool must be driven by that Channel.Tavg output, while FuelPin.Qcool drives the same Channel.Q_fuel input. This is inferred from the port table and local heat balance: the pin needs the channel's average coolant temperature for heat transfer, and the channel needs the pin's removed heat. Episodes 2, 4, and 6 show this pattern in models that build and conserve; Episode 3's attempt to feed fp2.Tcool from ch1.Tavg worsened Tf2 without fixing T2.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin.Tcool is driven by Const.y, another Channel.Tavg, or Channel.Tin; or Channel.Q_fuel is not driven by the paired FuelPin.Qcool.
items.recommended_strategy: Check each FuelPin/Channel pair as a two-way thermal coupling: connect(<fuelpin>.Qcool, <channel>.Q_fuel) and connect(<channel>.Tavg, <fuelpin>.Tcool). Do not substitute Channel.Tin or Channel.Tout for Tcool.
known_pitfalls: Channel.Tin is an input and cannot be a source for FuelPin.Tcool.
Using an upstream Channel.Tavg for a downstream FuelPin breaks the local conjugate heat-transfer pairing.

items.title: Mixer mass inputs need branch flows, not Mixer.m
items.description: In parallel plants with Splitter and Mixer, Mixer.m1 and Mixer.m2 must be driven by the corresponding branch mass-flow outputs, typically Splitter.m1/m2 or downstream Splitter branch flows. Episode 5 had connect(mix1.m, mix1.m2), a self-referential mass input from the Mixer output, causing nonlinear solve failure at time=0 even though all inputs were connected. This is a structural/physical routing error, not a tool-format error.
items.problem_signature: Simulation fails solving a nonlinear system at time=0; a Mixer.m input is connected to Mixer.m or another Mixer output instead of a Splitter branch mass flow.
items.recommended_strategy: Trace mass from the inlet Const.mdot through Splitter.m and Splitter.m1/m2 to Channel.mdot and Mixer.m1/m2. Replace any Mixer.m -> Mixer.mN connection with the matching Splitter branch mass output.
known_pitfalls: Mixer.T and Mixer.m are outputs; they cannot drive Mixer.T1/T2/m1/m2 inputs.
Do not use Channel.Tout or Channel.Tavg as a mass-flow source.

items.title: Port names are typed: T, m, Q are distinct
items.description: In Splitter/Mixer/Channel/FuelPin assembly, temperature, mass-flow, and heat ports are not interchangeable even if all are scalar connectors. Episode 1 repeatedly connected temperature outputs such as Channel.Tout/Tavg or Splitter.T1 to Mixer.T/m inputs and used Mixer.T/m as if they were inputs; final model still had ch1.Tout driving split1.m and Mixer.m driving Splitter.m. This produces over/under-determined or physically meaningless models.
items.problem_signature: Connections mix T outputs with m inputs, m outputs with T inputs, or Q outputs with non-heat inputs; build reports too many/few equations or nonlinear solve failure.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding connections, build three separate signal maps: temperature path, mass-flow path, and heat path. For each input, choose a source with the same physical quantity and with output direction from the port table.
known_pitfalls: Mixer.T and Mixer.m are outputs, not inputs; Mixer inputs are T1,m1,T2,m2.
Splitter.T and Splitter.m are inputs; Splitter outputs are T1,m1,T2,m2.
Channel.Tout/Tavg are temperature outputs and must never drive mdot or m inputs.

items.title: Tuning requires changing the offending parameter
items.description: In tune tasks where global targets Tin, mdot, Tmix, and mmix already match, changing the global Const.mdot cannot fix a single FuelPin temperature error and will break the matched global flow target. Episodes 2 and 4 diagnosed wrong_parameter but submitted with unchanged parameters; Episode 4 also tried mdot.k=19500, which made mdot 18.18% off while the isolated Tf2 error remained about 20%. The goal error persisted because the out-of-spec local parameter was not adjusted.
items.problem_signature: compare_to_targets shows only one local Tf or branch temperature off while Tin, mdot, Tmix/mmix, and other channel outlets match; agent sets a global boundary parameter to its current value or submits after diagnosis only.
items.recommended_strategy: Use compare_to_targets to localize the affected FuelPin/Channel stage, then set a parameter on that local component or its PowerSource and rerun. Do not alter global Const.mdot or Const.tin when their measured values already match targets.
known_pitfalls: Setting a parameter to its existing value is a no-op.
Recording diagnose('wrong_parameter') is not a repair action.
Global flow changes perturb all channel outlet temperatures and fuel temperatures, not just one local Tf.

items.title: FuelPin heat and coolant feedback ports
items.description: In assembly/repair tasks with FuelPin and Channel components, FuelPin.Qcool is the heat-flow output that must drive Channel.Q_fuel, while Channel.Tavg is the coolant-temperature output that must drive FuelPin.Tcool. This follows from the port table and conservation roles: Qcool is generated heat removed to coolant, Q_fuel is channel heat input, and Tcool needs the channel bulk/average coolant temperature. It does not apply to tasks where a Sensor or alternate component is explicitly intended to mediate the measured temperature, but the source must still be an output of compatible physical meaning.
items.problem_signature: Unconnected ch.Q_fuel or fp.Tcool; attempts like fp.Tcool -> ch.Q_fuel or ch.Q_fuel -> fp.Tcool rejected as input-to-input.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding connections, classify each port as input or output from the table; connect only output -> input. For each FuelPin/Channel pair, use FuelPin.Qcool -> Channel.Q_fuel and Channel.Tavg -> FuelPin.Tcool unless a task-specific sensor path is required.
known_pitfalls: Treating FuelPin.Tcool as a source because it sounds like a temperature output.
Treating Channel.Q_fuel as a source because it is heat-related.
Using Channel.Tout for FuelPin.Tcool in loop/parallel plants when the design point and conservation checks imply average coolant temperature feedback.

items.title: Duplicate connections create overdetermined models
items.description: In assembly tasks, adding a connection that already exists or adding a second driver to an input can change an underdetermined model into an overdetermined one even when the port table reports all inputs connected. The requirement is that every input connector is driven exactly once; outputs may fan out, but inputs may not be multiply driven. This does not apply when a rejected duplicate call made no model change, or when the task explicitly permits algebraic redundant sensors.
items.problem_signature: add_connect reports duplicate or all inputs connected, then run_simulation reports too many equations/over-determined system.
items.recommended_strategy: Maintain a connection ledger from the initial model plus accepted add_connect results. Before each add_connect, remove pairs already present and verify that no target input already has a driver. If overdetermined, delete or avoid the duplicate driver rather than adding more connections.
action_template: for each candidate pair: reject if target input already driven
known_pitfalls: Re-adding initial-model connections after inspect.
Assuming duplicate rejection is harmless when a previous accepted call already added the same edge.
Confusing 'all inputs connected' with 'all equations balanced'; duplicate edges can still overconstrain the system.

items.title: No-op parameter writes do not tune
items.description: In tuning tasks, setting a parameter to its current value is a no-op and cannot move an off-design operating point. Episodes 1 and 6 show mdot.k already equal to the measured/target flow, yet the agent set it to the same value and resubmitted unchanged models. This does not apply when the parameter value differs from the current model value or when the measured flow is off target.
items.problem_signature: compare_to_targets shows some targets off; set_parameter uses the same value already in the model; rerun gives identical outputs.
items.recommended_strategy: Read current parameter values from the model, compare measured quantities to targets, and choose a parameter that is both currently off specification and causally able to move the off-target measures. After each set_parameter, rerun and verify that at least one measured value changes.
action_template: if value == current_value: choose different parameter or new value
known_pitfalls: Setting mdot.k to the target when measured mdot is already on target.
Recording a generic wrong_parameter diagnosis without identifying which parameter is wrong.
Submitting after an unchanged rerun.

items.title: Splitter and Mixer flow ports are paired
items.description: In parallel assembly tasks with Splitter and Mixer components, temperature and mass-flow signals must be routed as paired quantities: Splitter.T1/T2 drive channel or mixer temperature inputs, and Splitter.m1/m2 drive corresponding mass-flow inputs. Mixer.T and Mixer.m are outputs, not inputs, so connecting Channel.Tout -> Mixer.T or Channel.Tout -> Mixer.m is invalid. This does not apply to components with different port tables, but the output-to-input and physical-pairing checks are general.
items.problem_signature: Repeated errors 'both are outputs' for Mixer.T/Mixer.m, or unconnected mix1.m1/m2 while splitter mass outputs exist.
items.recommended_strategy: For each branch, map Splitter.Ti to the branch Channel.Tin or Mixer.Ti, and Splitter.mi to the branch Channel.mdot or Mixer.mi. Use Mixer.T/Mixer.m only as downstream outputs, e.g. as a mixed temperature source to another Mixer.T input when the topology requires cascaded mixing.
known_pitfalls: Using Mixer.T or Mixer.m as if they were input ports.
Driving Channel.Tin from a Const when a Splitter.T output is required by the parallel topology.
Leaving Mixer.m1/m2 unconnected while only temperature outputs are connected.

items.title: Sensor input must be driven by measured output
items.description: In sensor-loop assembly tasks, a Sensor.y output may drive a downstream input such as SteamGenerator.Tin, but Sensor.y_in itself still requires exactly one source. If the measured hot-leg temperature is Channel.Tout, then Channel.Tout must drive Sensor.y_in; leaving y_in unconnected yields an underdetermined model. This does not apply when the sensor is absent or when another explicit measured output is designated by the task.
items.problem_signature: Initial model has connect(sens.y, sg.Tin), but inspect reports sens.y_in unconnected and simulation is underdetermined.
items.recommended_strategy: Treat the Sensor as a pass-through measurement element: connect the physical output to Sensor.y_in, then connect Sensor.y to the component input that should receive the sensed value. Do not repeatedly add the already-existing Sensor.y -> downstream input edge.
known_pitfalls: Assuming a Sensor output connection also satisfies its own input connector.
Trying to reconnect sens.y -> sg.Tin when that edge is already in the initial model.
Submitting with unconnected sens.y_in despite a build failure.

items.title: Loop heat and temperature routing
items.description: In loop/sensor_loop plants with FuelPin, Channel, SteamGenerator, and optional Sensor, the heat path is PowerSource.P -> FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Qcool -> Channel.Q_fuel, and Channel.Tout -> SteamGenerator.Tin (possibly through Sensor.y_in/Sensor.y). The coolant return path is SteamGenerator.Tout -> Channel.Tin, and FuelPin.Tcool must see Channel.Tavg. This follows from the port table and conservation laws: Channel.Q_fuel is a heat input, SteamGenerator.Tin is a temperature input, and FuelPin coolant temperature should be the channel average, not inlet or outlet.
items.problem_signature: Qfuel near zero or enormous temperatures; physics failures in fp:energy/ch:energy; or all inputs connected but heat/temperature signals are swapped.
items.recommended_strategy: Before simulating, audit each connection by port direction and physical quantity: power outputs drive heat inputs, temperature outputs drive temperature inputs, and flow outputs drive mdot inputs. For a loop, explicitly verify the closed sequence Channel.Tout -> Sensor/SteamGenerator.Tin -> SteamGenerator.Tout -> Channel.Tin and the fuel heat chain PowerSource -> FuelPin -> Channel.
known_pitfalls: Connecting Sensor.y to Channel.Q_fuel confuses a sensed temperature with heat power.
Connecting FuelPin.Qcool to SteamGenerator.Tin confuses heat power with coolant inlet temperature.
Using Channel.Tin or Channel.Tout for FuelPin.Tcool instead of Channel.Tavg changes fuel/clad temperatures.
Omitting SteamGenerator.Tout -> Channel.Tin breaks the recirculating loop boundary condition.

items.title: Input-to-input connect attempts
items.description: In assembly/repair tasks, repeated add_connect calls such as <input> -> <input> fail because connections must be output -> input. Episodes show this with fp.Tcool -> ch.Tin and ch.Q_fuel -> ch.Q_fuel; the latter also leaves the model under-determined because no source drives Channel.Q_fuel.
items.problem_signature: Tool error 'both are inputs; a connection must go output -> input', duplicate connection errors, or BUILD FAILED 'Too few equations' after trying to connect an unconnected input to itself.
items.recommended_strategy: Use the port table to classify each endpoint first. For every unconnected input, choose a compatible output from another component; never use an input port as the first element of a connect pair. If the same input-to-input call fails twice, stop and re-read the port table instead of retrying.
action_template: for each unconnected input <target>.<input_port>: select <source>.<output_port> with matching physical quantity
known_pitfalls: Treating replace_connect old/new pairs as unordered aliases; the first element must still be an output.
Removing and re-adding an already valid connection does not fix a different missing input.
A diagnosis label typo such as 'missing-connection' is a tool/format error, not a plant fault.

items.title: Splitter flow input needs Const.y
items.description: In parallel2 plants with Splitter and Mixer, Splitter.m is an input and must be driven by the flow Const.y output; Splitter.T is driven by the inlet temperature Const.y. The successful episode added mdot.y -> split1.m and immediately met all targets with conservation checks passing. This is a structural mass-flow boundary rule, not an instance-specific recipe.
items.problem_signature: All branch temperatures and mass fractions are wired, but Splitter.m is unconnected; mmix or mdot target cannot be established.
items.recommended_strategy: When a Splitter has T and m inputs, connect the temperature boundary Const.y to Splitter.T and the mass-flow boundary Const.y to Splitter.m. Then verify branch outputs T1/m1 and T2/m2 drive the corresponding Channel.Tin/mdot and Mixer.m1/m2 inputs.
known_pitfalls: Assuming Splitter.m is an output because m1/m2 are outputs.
Driving Mixer.m1/m2 from branch flows while leaving Splitter.m unconnected.

items.title: Balanced physics is not goal success
items.description: In sensor_loop multistep repair, the plant was structurally valid, steady, and all component conservation checks passed, but every temperature was about 15 K below target while Qsg, Qfuel, and mdot were on target. Re-setting unchanged FuelPin conductances did not change the result; this is a goal/boundary-condition error, not a physics imbalance or missing connection.
items.problem_signature: check_physics PASS and compare_to_targets shows a uniform temperature offset with heat flows and mdot already correct.
items.recommended_strategy: When conservation passes but temperatures are uniformly offset, treat it as a boundary/parameter tuning problem: inspect SteamGenerator secondary temperature/UA or other thermal boundary parameters, change one parameter, simulate, and compare. Do not repeat set_parameter with the same value or keep recording generic diagnoses.
action_template: if physics PASS and temperatures uniformly offset: inspect thermal boundary parameters such as <steamgenerator>.Tsec or <steamgenerator>.UA
known_pitfalls: Calling set_parameter with the current value and expecting a new operating point.
Classifying a uniform temperature offset as a structural missing connection when all inputs are connected and conservation passes.
Using invalid diagnose labels such as 'temperature deviation' instead of the allowed labels.

items.title: Port-table-first structural audit
items.description: For assemble/repair tasks, first inspect the port table and enumerate all input connectors, then add only output -> input connections with matching physical quantities.
