The successful parallel2 episode fixed the single missing Splitter.m input and then verified simulation, physics, and targets before submitting; failed episodes skipped or corrupted this audit and ended with build or physics failures.
items.problem_signature: Unconnected inputs remain, duplicate connections are attempted, or the model builds but has nonphysical temperatures/heat flows.
items.recommended_strategy: Perform an ordered audit: inspect port table; list unconnected inputs; map each input to one compatible output; add connections in one batch; run simulation; check physics; compare targets; only then submit. If a tool reports a format or direction error, correct the call class before changing plant parameters.
known_pitfalls: Submitting after only 'All inputs connected' without physics and target checks.
Mixing tool/format errors with structural faults and changing parameters in response.
Using diagnose labels as a substitute for reading the port table.

items.title: Series channels cascade Tout to Tin
items.description: In series Channel assemblies, the upstream Channel.Tout must drive the next downstream Channel.Tin; only the first Channel.Tin is driven by the inlet Const. This follows from mass/energy continuity along a single coolant path. Episode 1 had ch1.Tout -> ch2.Tin and all non-fuel targets matched; episode 3 drove every Channel.Tin from tin.y and downstream outlet temperatures collapsed toward the inlet value.
items.problem_signature: First stage outlet is on target but later stage outlet temperatures are too low or equal to the inlet temperature.
items.recommended_strategy: Wire the inlet Const only to the first Channel.Tin, then connect each upstream Channel.Tout to the next Channel.Tin in order.
known_pitfalls: Fan-out of the inlet Const to every Channel.Tin creates parallel independent heating from the same boundary, not a series temperature rise.
This rule does not apply to parallel branches, where Splitter.T1/T2 should drive branch Channel.Tin.

items.title: Loop SteamGenerator needs same mdot
items.description: In a recirculating Channel/SteamGenerator loop, SteamGenerator.mdot must be driven by the same flow Const as Channel.mdot. The SteamGenerator removes heat from the same coolant stream, so its mass-flow input cannot be left unconnected or driven by a temperature signal. Episode 6 succeeded by adding mdot.y -> sg.mdot; episode 2 produced Thot_s = 18000 by connecting mdot.y to Sensor.y_in and had severe energy failures with wrong routing.
items.problem_signature: Unconnected sg.mdot, or a sensor output equal to the numeric flow value, with nonphysical temperatures and failed ch/fp energy checks.
items.recommended_strategy: Connect the flow Const output to both Channel.mdot and SteamGenerator.mdot; connect the Sensor.y_in to the temperature output being measured, not to a flow Const.
known_pitfalls: A Sensor.y_in fed by mdot.y reports the flow value as a temperature measurement.
Do not self-connect Channel.Tavg to Channel.Tin to satisfy an unconnected input; that creates an algebraic shortcut instead of the loop return path.

items.title: Rewriting unchanged parameters is no tuning
items.description: In tune tasks, setting a parameter to its current value is a no-op even if the tool reports OK. Episodes 1 and 4 repeatedly rewrote FuelPin G_gap/G_cl or mdot.k to the existing values and the simulated operating point did not change; episode 5 succeeded only when mdot.k was changed from 90000 to the target 19500.
items.problem_signature: set_parameter OK followed by identical run_simulation and compare_to_targets values.
items.recommended_strategy: Before setting a parameter, compare the requested value with the current model value; if unchanged, choose a different value or a different parameter and rerun simulation/comparison.
action_template: if value == current value then choose a changed candidate
known_pitfalls: Do not infer that a parameter is irrelevant from a no-op set; the simulation never tested a new value.
Diagnose labels are restricted; invalid labels such as fuel_pin_conductance or fp:energy are tool/format errors, not physics evidence.

items.title: Fix measured boundary flow first
items.description: For tune tasks with a Const driving flow, if measured mdot/mmix is off target while Tin and power are on target, set that Const.k to the target flow before changing heat-transfer parameters. Episode 5 demonstrated this: changing mdot.k from 90000 to 19500 made Tmix, mmix, T1, T2, Tf1, and Tf2 all meet targets with conservation passing.
items.problem_signature: Measured mdot/mmix is far off target and coolant temperature rise is too small or too large while boundary Tin is correct.
items.recommended_strategy: Set the flow Const.k to the design mdot, rerun simulation, compare all targets, then check physics; only tune FuelPin conductances if fuel temperatures remain off after flow and coolant temperatures are correct.
known_pitfalls: Do not tune FuelPin G_gap/G_cl when mdot itself is off target; coolant enthalpy rise is dominated by flow.
This does not apply when mdot is already on target and only one fuel temperature is off.

items.title: Mixer temperature inputs need branch Tout
items.description: In parallel plants with Splitter, Channel, and Mixer components, each Mixer.T1/T2 input must be driven by the corresponding Channel.Tout output, not by a Splitter temperature output or left unconnected. The Mixer combines branch outlet temperatures with branch mass flows; using an inlet temperature or omitting one branch breaks energy balance or leaves the design point unreachable. This applies to parallel and nested-parallel topologies where Mixer.T1/T2 represent heated branch outlets; it does not apply to Mixer.m1/m2, which should see the corresponding Splitter mass outputs.
items.problem_signature: Mixer.T1 or Mixer.T2 unconnected, or Tmix/Tout targets off while branch mass flows are already correct
items.recommended_strategy: For each heated branch, trace Channel.Tin and Channel.mdot from the Splitter, then connect that same Channel.Tout to the Mixer temperature input paired with the same branch mass flow. Verify all Mixer inputs are driven exactly once and run physics conservation checks.
known_pitfalls: Connecting Splitter.T1/T2 to Mixer.T1/T2 instead of Channel.Tout
Leaving one Mixer temperature input unconnected while all mass inputs are connected
Pairing a branch outlet temperature with the wrong branch mass flow

items.title: Nested splitters must feed channel Tin
items.description: In parallel3-style plants with two Splitter components, a downstream Splitter.T output is the inlet temperature source for channels on that downstream branch. If a Channel.Tin input is missing while its Channel.mdot is driven by the downstream Splitter, the plant may still compile but the thermal state is wrong or initialization can become inconsistent. This applies when a second Splitter receives split1.T2/split1.m2 and distributes flow to multiple Channels; it does not apply to series plants where Channel.Tin should come from the previous Channel.Tout.
items.problem_signature: A Channel.mdot is connected from split2.m1 or split2.m2 but the same Channel.Tin is unconnected
items.recommended_strategy: For every Channel whose mdot comes from a Splitter branch, connect the corresponding Splitter.T branch output to that Channel.Tin. In nested splitters, use the downstream Splitter.T1/T2 outputs for downstream channels, not the upstream Splitter.T2 unless that upstream output is explicitly the downstream Splitter.T input.
known_pitfalls: Driving Channel.mdot but forgetting Channel.Tin
Using an input port such as Channel.mdot as a connection source
Assuming upstream Splitter.T2 can directly feed all downstream channels when a second Splitter is present

items.title: Replacing a wrong link can expose another missing input
items.description: In repair tasks with Channel and FuelPin components, replacing a misrouted connection can remove the only driver from an input port and create a new structural fault. Episode 3 replaced fp2.Qcool -> ch1.mdot with fp2.Qcool -> ch2.Q_fuel, but then ch1.mdot was unconnected; repeated attempts to connect ch1.mdot -> ch2.mdot were tool/format errors because both are inputs. This failure class is structural plus tool/format, not a physics imbalance; it does not apply when the replacement leaves all input connectors driven exactly once.
items.problem_signature: replace_connect reports 'Unconnected inputs: <component>.<input>' followed by add_connect attempts using an input as the source
items.recommended_strategy: After every replace_connect, re-read the connection list and immediately drive any newly unconnected input from a valid output port. For Channel.mdot in series plants, use the Const.y mass-flow output; for Channel.Q_fuel, use the paired FuelPin.Qcool output; never use another Channel input as a source.
known_pitfalls: Treating an input-to-input connection as a valid way to propagate mass flow
Ignoring the 'Unconnected inputs' message after a replacement
Duplicating an existing connection instead of repairing the missing input

items.title: Do not tune unchanged parameters when Qfuel is off
items.description: In tuning tasks with PowerSource, FuelPin, and Channel components, if Qfuel is far from target and equals PowerSource.P0, the dominant fault is the PowerSource power parameter, not FuelPin conductances or already-correct boundary constants. Episode 4 repeatedly set mdot.k, fp.G_gap, and fp.G_cl to their existing values while Qfuel stayed at 1.5e+10, so Tout, Tavg, Tf, and Tc remained off and temperature bounds failed. This is a goal/parameter-selection error; it does not apply when Qfuel is already within tolerance and only fuel temperatures are off.
items.problem_signature: Qfuel target off by a large factor while Tin and mdot are already OK; set_parameter calls use values equal to current values
items.recommended_strategy: First compare measured Qfuel with the target and inspect PowerSource.P0. If Qfuel tracks P0 and is off, change PowerSource.P0 toward the Qfuel target, then rerun simulation and compare all thermal targets before tuning FuelPin.G_gap or G_cl.
known_pitfalls: Re-setting a parameter to its current value and expecting a new operating point
Tuning FuelPin conductances when the heat source magnitude is wrong
Ignoring physics bounds failures caused by excessive power

items.title: One-connection repair then full verification works
items.description: For repair tasks where the plant compiles but misses the design point, a single missing or wrong connection can be sufficient to restore all targets. Episodes 1, 5, and 6 succeeded by adding or replacing exactly one connection, then running simulation, physics conservation, and target comparison before submit. This method works when the initial model is structurally near-complete and measured non-target variables already match; it does not apply to tuning tasks with wrong parameter magnitudes or to repairs with multiple independent faults.
items.problem_signature: All inputs connected or one input missing; most boundary and mass-flow targets OK; one local connection is inconsistent with component-type port roles
items.recommended_strategy: Inspect the port table and current connections, identify the single input whose source violates the component-type rule, add or replace that connection, then verify in order: simulation, physics conservation, target comparison, submit. Avoid parameter changes until structural checks pass.
known_pitfalls: Submitting after target comparison without physics conservation checks
Changing parameters before checking structural completeness
Using duplicate connections or input-to-input connections during repair

items.title: Duplicate input drivers over-determine the model
items.description: In repair and multistep tasks, adding a second connection to an already driven input can produce a build failure with 'Too many equations, over-determined system' even when the tool reports all inputs connected. Episodes 1 and 4 show this after adding extra connections to Channel.Tin or FuelPin.Tcool while the original driver remained. This is a structural/tool-use failure, not a physics imbalance; it does not apply when the old connection has first been removed or replaced atomically.
items.problem_signature: Build failed with too many equations / over-determined system after add_connect; duplicate connection rejected but another new connection still added.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding a connection, read the current equation list and count drivers for the target input. Use replace_connect for a one-for-one source change; if add_connect is used, remove the old driver first and re-run the build immediately.
known_pitfalls: A batch add_connect can partially succeed: one duplicate is rejected while another extra driver is accepted.
The message 'All inputs connected' does not mean 'each input connected exactly once'.
Removing the wrong duplicate can leave an input unconnected and create a different structural failure.

items.title: Tune by target residuals, not labels
items.description: For tuning tasks where the plant builds and conserves mass/energy but some measured values are off, first classify which residuals are global versus local. Episode 2 succeeded by changing PowerSource.P0 when all temperatures and Qsg/Qfuel were high together; Episodes 3 and 6 failed by changing FuelPin conductances or flow without achieving the target Tf/Tc, and Episode 5 repeatedly reset unchanged power parameters while all temperatures remained high. This procedure does not apply when structural checks fail, when inputs are unconnected, or when physics conservation checks fail.
items.problem_signature: Simulation OK and conservation PASS, but compare_to_targets shows a coherent group of residuals; repeated set_parameter calls leave outputs unchanged or only partially corrected.
items.recommended_strategy: Run simulation, compare_to_targets, and check_physics before editing. If Qfuel/Qsg and all coolant/fuel temperatures are high together, test PowerSource.P0 first; if only fuel/clad temperatures are off while coolant temperatures and heat flows match, tune FuelPin G_gap/G_cl. After every parameter change, rerun compare_to_targets and do not submit until all targets are OK.
known_pitfalls: Setting a parameter to its current value is a no-op and cannot repair a wrong operating point.
Diagnose labels are restricted; invalid labels are tool/format errors and do not repair the model.
A physics PASS only means conservation/bounds are satisfied; it does not mean the design point is met.

items.title: Do not submit after partial target match
items.description: In tuning tasks, submitting after only some targets pass is a goal error even if build, simulation, structural, and physics checks pass. Episode 6 submitted with Tf2 still off target after a conductance change; Episode 3 ended with Tf and Tc off target; Episode 5 ended with all temperatures off and a bounds:temperature physics failure. This does not apply when compare_to_targets explicitly reports every design measure within tolerance and check_physics passes.
items.problem_signature: Final verifier goal_ok=false despite build_ok/sim_ok/structural_ok/physics_ok=true, or compare_to_targets still lists OFF entries before submit.
items.recommended_strategy: Treat compare_to_targets as a gate: enumerate every OFF measure, adjust the parameter class that affects those residuals, rerun simulation and comparison, and only submit when all target rows are OK and check_physics has no failures.
action_template: if any OFF: set_parameter(instance=<component>, parameter=<name>, value=<candidate>)
submit() only if all targets OK
known_pitfalls: A single changed parameter can move one residual into tolerance while leaving another residual outside tolerance.
check_physics PASS is necessary but not sufficient for goal_ok.
Repeated no-op edits or no-op file edits can create the appearance of progress without changing the operating point.

items.title: Each input connector has exactly one output driver
items.description: In assemble and repair tasks with typed connector ports, every input connector must be driven exactly once by an output connector. Adding a second connection to an already driven input creates an over-determined system even if the port table still reports no unconnected inputs; this is a structural error, not a physics or goal error. The fix is to remove the wrong driver first, then connect the intended output to that input.
items.problem_signature: BUILD FAILED: Too many equations / over-determined system after add_connect, while all inputs are connected.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding a connection, inspect the current connection ledger for the target input. If it already has a driver, use replace_connect or remove_connect on that exact old pair, then add the intended output->input pair. Never add a second driver to satisfy a suspected missing source.
known_pitfalls: Treating 'Unconnected inputs: none' as proof that the topology is valid.
Re-adding the same connection after removing it without changing the rest of the ledger.
Using an input port as a source; connections must be output -> input.

items.title: FuelPin.Q_fission needs PowerSource.P, not temperature or power-like substitutes
items.description: In single, parallel, and loop plants containing FuelPin and PowerSource, FuelPin.Q_fission is the fission heat input and must be driven by PowerSource.P. Episodes 1, 3, and 6 show that driving Q_fission from Const.y, Channel.Tavg, or leaving it effectively misrouted produces temperatures or heat flows of order 1e9, failed energy/gap/ordering checks, or wrong Qfuel. This is a structural routing rule inferred from the port table and conservation behavior, not a claim about a hidden reference answer.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin temperatures or Qfuel are ~1e9, or Qfuel is near zero, while PowerSource.P is connected to a temperature input or Channel.Tin.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin, verify Q_fission is driven by PowerSource.P. If PowerSource.P is currently connected to a temperature or flow input, remove that wrong connection and replace it with the correct Q_fission driver while preserving the one-driver-per-input ledger.
known_pitfalls: Adding PowerSource.P -> FuelPin.Q_fission without removing the existing wrong PowerSource.P connection.
Confusing FuelPin.Qcool with FuelPin.Q_fission; Qcool is an output to Channel.Q_fuel.
Using Channel.Tavg as a heat source for Q_fission.

items.title: FuelPin.Tcool needs Channel.Tavg, not PowerSource.P or FuelPin.Tc
items.description: For FuelPin/Channel thermal feedback, FuelPin.Tcool must see the coolant temperature represented by Channel.Tavg. Episode 3 showed that connecting FuelPin.Tc to FuelPin.Tcool creates self-feedback with Qfuel=0 and very high fuel temperatures; episodes 3 and 6 showed that connecting PowerSource.P to FuelPin.Tcool makes Tf and Tc equal the power magnitude. Episode 5 succeeded with Channel.Tavg -> FuelPin.Tcool in a loop plant. This is a component-type routing rule inferred from port semantics and simulated conservation checks.
items.problem_signature: Tf/Tc are ~power magnitude, Qfuel is zero, or fp:gap_law/fp:ordering fails while Tcool is not driven by Channel.Tavg.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin paired with a Channel, check that the Channel.Tavg output drives that FuelPin.Tcool input. If Tcool is self-driven by FuelPin.Tc or driven by PowerSource.P, remove that connection and connect the corresponding Channel.Tavg instead.
known_pitfalls: Using Channel.Tin instead of Channel.Tavg for FuelPin.Tcool.
Using FuelPin.Tc as its own coolant boundary, which creates algebraic self-feedback.
In parallel plants, cross-connecting ch1.Tavg to fp2.Tcool while leaving fp1.Tcool wrong.

items.title: Channel.Tin and Channel.mdot need temperature and flow sources
items.description: Channel.Tin must be driven by a temperature signal such as Const.y, Splitter.T1/T2, or SteamGenerator.Tout depending on topology; Channel.mdot must be driven by a flow signal such as Const.y or Splitter.m1/m2. Episode 1 showed PowerSource.P -> Channel.Tin makes Tout/Tavg/Tf/Tc equal the power magnitude; episode 4 showed Channel.Tout -> Channel.mdot corrupts branch flow and mixer temperature. This is a structural and physical routing rule inferred from port names and observed energy/temperature failures.
items.problem_signature: Channel temperatures are ~power magnitude, branch Tmix is extreme, or a Channel.mdot input is driven by a temperature output.
items.recommended_strategy: Classify each Channel input by physical quantity before editing: Tin is temperature, mdot is mass flow, Q_fuel is heat. Replace any heat-to-temperature, temperature-to-flow, or power-to-boundary connection with the appropriate temperature or flow output, preserving one driver per input.
known_pitfalls: Connecting PowerSource.P to Channel.Tin because both are scalar connectors.
Connecting Channel.Tout to Channel.mdot in parallel plants.
Trying to connect an input such as Channel.mdot to Mixer.m2; both are inputs.

items.title: FuelPin coolant feedback uses Channel.Tavg
items.description: In assembly or repair tasks with FuelPin and Channel components, FuelPin.Tcool must be driven by Channel.Tavg, not Channel.Tin or Channel.Tout. Episode 1's complete wiring met all targets and conservation checks with ch.Tavg->fp.Tcool; Episode 4's attempted replacement to ch.Tin left fp.Tcool unconnected and did not improve the failed physics. This is inferred from the port table and supported by the successful simulated design point.
items.problem_signature: FuelPin.Tcool unconnected or connected from Channel.Tin/Tout; fuel temperatures off while coolant outlet may remain plausible.
items.recommended_strategy: For each FuelPin/Channel heat pair, connect the Channel.Tavg output to the paired FuelPin.Tcool input; verify with inspect that no input remains unconnected and with check_physics that FuelPin energy and gap-law checks pass.
known_pitfalls: Do not connect <fuelpin>.Tcool to <channel>.Tin: both are inputs.
Do not use <channel>.Tout for Tcool unless a task explicitly defines that feedback law; the successful single-plant evidence uses Tavg.

items.title: Mixer flow inputs need Splitter mass outputs
items.description: In parallel assembly tasks with Splitter and Mixer components, Mixer.T1/T2/m1/m2 are inputs and must be driven by upstream outputs, not by Mixer.T/m outputs or Channel.mdot inputs. Episodes 3 and 5 show repeated rejected connections such as ch1.mdot->mix1.m1, tin.y->mix1.T, and mix1.m->mix1.m1, followed by unconnected mixer inputs or overdetermined builds. The structural signature is a build failure with too few or too many equations plus unconnected Mixer.m1/m2 inputs.
items.problem_signature: add_connect says 'both are inputs' or 'both are outputs' for Mixer ports; verifier lists mix*.m1/m2 unconnected; build is under- or over-determined.
items.recommended_strategy: Before adding connections, classify every port from the table. Drive Splitter.T/m from boundary Const outputs, drive Channel.Tin/mdot from Splitter.T*/m* outputs, and drive Mixer.T1/T2/m1/m2 from the corresponding branch Channel.Tout and Splitter.m* outputs; avoid duplicate drivers on any Mixer input.
known_pitfalls: Mixer.T and Mixer.m are outputs; do not connect them back into Mixer.T1/m1.
Channel.mdot is an input; it cannot drive Mixer.m1.
Duplicate connections to the same Mixer input can create over-determined systems.

items.title: Do not tune conductances for power deficits
items.description: In tuning tasks where a downstream Channel outlet temperature and FuelPin fuel temperature are both low while upstream stages match targets, changing FuelPin.G_gap or G_cl is not an effective fix for a missing power level. Episode 6 showed G_cl changes barely moved T3/Tf3, while increasing ps3.P0 from 2e8 to 2e9 moved T3 from 619.029 to 635.513 and Tf3 from 644.447 to 883.022; Episode 2 similarly showed G_gap/G_cl changes moving Tf in the wrong direction while Qfuel and coolant temperatures stayed fixed. This is a goal/parameter-selection error, not a structural or physics conservation failure.
items.problem_signature: check_physics passes conservation, but one stage's outlet and fuel temperatures are far below target; conductance sweeps produce small or opposite changes; Qfuel or stage power is suspect.
items.recommended_strategy: First compare which measured quantities are off. If both coolant outlet temperature and fuel temperature for a stage are low and conservation passes, inspect the stage PowerSource.P0/Q_fission level before changing FuelPin conductances; use a parameter sweep on P0 and re-run compare_to_targets. Only tune G_gap/G_cl when power and coolant temperatures are already consistent and only fuel/clad temperature drops need adjustment.
known_pitfalls: Increasing G_gap or G_cl can reduce fuel temperature when the target requires higher fuel temperature.
A correct diagnosis label is not a repair; still change the parameter that affects the off-target measure.
Do not infer a final parameter value is correct unless compare_to_targets shows all measures within tolerance.

items.title: Assemble single FuelPin-Channel plant canonically
items.description: For single-plant assembly tasks with PowerSource, FuelPin, Channel, and two Const boundary sources, the demonstrated successful procedure is to inspect the port table, add the three missing heat/feedback connections, then verify simulation, physics, and targets before submitting. Episode 1 achieved exact target agreement and all conservation checks with this ordered method. This skill applies when the initial model already has tin.y->ch.Tin and mdot.y->ch.mdot and the remaining unconnected inputs are fp.Q_fission, fp.Tcool, and ch.Q_fuel.
items.problem_signature: Single plant with exactly three unconnected inputs: FuelPin.Q_fission, FuelPin.Tcool, Channel.Q_fuel.
items.recommended_strategy: Use the port table to confirm output-to-input direction, add only the canonical three connections, then run simulation, check_physics, and compare_to_targets; submit only if all are OK.
known_pitfalls: Do not add duplicate boundary connections already present in the initial model.
Do not submit after only 'All inputs connected'; physics and target checks are required.

items.title: Series channels need upstream Tout as Tin
items.description: In series2 assembly tasks with two Channel stages, a downstream Channel.Tin must be driven by the upstream Channel.Tout, not by the inlet Const.y, when the design point gives a higher second-stage outlet temperature. The trajectory showed that feeding the same Const.y to both Channel.Tin inputs made T2 equal T1 while T1 and Tf1 matched; by energy balance, the second stage needs the first-stage heated outlet as its inlet. This is an inference from the port table, conservation laws, and the observed T2/Tf2 mismatch, not a verified reference connection.
items.problem_signature: All inputs connected and conservation passes, but downstream stage outlet/fuel temperatures are too low and equal or near the first-stage values.
items.recommended_strategy: For series thermal-hydraulic stages, check whether the downstream Channel.Tin is connected to upstream Channel.Tout. If both stages receive the same inlet Const.y, replace the downstream inlet connection with the upstream outlet and rerun target comparison.
known_pitfalls: Do not use replace_connect with identical old and new pairs; that is a no-op tool/format error.
Do not diagnose this as a physics conservation failure when check_physics passes; it is a structural routing/goal error.
Do not apply to parallel branches where both channels are intended to share the same inlet boundary.

items.title: Isolated high Tf indicates FuelPin conductance tuning
items.description: In loop tuning tasks with PowerSource, FuelPin, Channel, SteamGenerator, and Const.mdot, if Thot, Tcold, Tc, Qsg, Qfuel, and mdot already match but Tf is far too high, the fault is in FuelPin conductance parameters, not PowerSource.P0 or boundary conditions. Episodes 2 and 4 showed that increasing PowerSource.P0 by 10x changed all temperatures and heat flows away from target while leaving the isolated Tf problem unresolved. The correct class of action is to adjust FuelPin G_gap/G_cl upward enough to reduce the fuel-to-clad temperature drop; the exact values are not established by these trajectories.
items.problem_signature: Target comparison has only Tf grossly off; coolant temperatures, Tc, Qsg, Qfuel, and mdot are within tolerance; check_physics may flag bounds:temperature due to excessive Tf.
items.recommended_strategy: Keep PowerSource.P0, SteamGenerator parameters, mdot, and loop connections fixed. Tune FuelPin G_gap and/or G_cl in the direction that lowers Tf, then rerun simulation, check_physics, and compare_to_targets after each change.
known_pitfalls: Setting a parameter to its current value is a no-op and will not change Tf.
Changing PowerSource.P0 when Qfuel and Qsg already match is a goal error that breaks heat balance targets.
Do not use this rule when Qfuel/Qsg or coolant temperatures are also off; then the boundary power, SG, mdot, or routing may be at fault.

items.title: No-op edits cannot repair routing or parameters
items.description: Across failed episodes, repeated replace_connect calls with identical old/new pairs and set_parameter calls with the current value produced OK/ERROR messages but no model change. This is a tool/format error class: the agent treated a recorded diagnosis or a no-op edit as if it repaired the plant. The signature is unchanged simulation and target-comparison outputs after an edit step.
items.problem_signature: replace_connect reports old and new identical, or set_parameter sets the same value already in the model; subsequent run_simulation and compare_to_targets are numerically unchanged.
items.recommended_strategy: Before editing, read the current model or connection list and choose a genuinely different source port or parameter value. After editing, verify that the model text changed; if outputs are identical, treat the edit as failed and formulate a different structural or parameter hypothesis.
known_pitfalls: Do not repeat the same replace_connect pair after a wrong_routing diagnosis.
Do not confuse a successful diagnose call with a repair action.
This does not apply when a deliberate re-run is used only to confirm reproducibility.
